task: Apply proposed_fix_sketch items 1 and 2 from decode-compiler-tree-deadline-swallow-finding.json: stop build_completion_forest from swallowing a cooperative decode-deadline TimeoutError as a fake empty-completion-forest grammar dead-end, and add check_decode_deadline() coverage to the compiler-tree per-position loop, matching model.twotower v261's LTR-repair/MaskGIT coverage.

summary: compiler_draft.py:build_completion_forest -- added `except TimeoutError: raise` before the pre-existing bare `except Exception: return CompletionForest((), "none")` around the GrammarCapabilityAdapterV1.completion_domain(request) call, so a cooperative-deadline TimeoutError (including one arriving from the eval harness's SIGALRM-style interval) propagates instead of being recorded as constrained_dead_ends with reason=empty_completion_forest.

twotower.py:_compiler_ltr_decode_one -- added a check_decode_deadline() call at the top of the per-position `while len(prefix) < length and prefix[-1] != eos_id:` loop (the same call/comment pattern already used by the LTR-repair loop at line ~4906 and the MaskGIT loop at line ~13266), so a deadline that expires between build_completion_forest calls -- not just inside one -- is still caught. _compiler_ltr_decode_batch calls _compiler_ltr_decode_one once per row, so both call sites are covered by the one loop edit.
change.why_safe: Both edits are purely about *when* an already-armed deadline raises, never about what the grammar considers legal: I6 (constrained legality) and I3 (deterministic decode) are untouched -- no candidate set, ranking, or bypass logic changes. The new TimeoutError re-raise only fires when a deadline was explicitly armed by set_decode_deadline (a caller opt-in); when unarmed, check_decode_deadline() is a no-op and completion_domain's non-timeout exceptions still fall through to the pre-existing fail-closed empty-forest path unchanged (regression-tested explicitly).
